title: Deterministic Approximation of Total Variation Distance in Product Spin Systems via Concurrent Lock-Free Kotlin Primitives
topic: Deterministic Approximation of the Total Variation Distance Between Spin Systems
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a deterministic algorithm for approximating the total variation distance (TVD) between two product spin systems. The method operates on binary spin vectors encoded as probability arrays and exploits a lock-free, atomic-increment scheme to aggregate per-spin contributions without contention. We prove that the algorithm preserves a linearizable invariant that bounds the TVD by a sum of per-spin discrepancies, yielding an asymptotic complexity of $O(n)$ for $n$ spins. The implementation is fully deterministic, requiring no randomization, and is expressed in Kotlin using atomic primitives from the standard library. Experimental validation on synthetic systems up to $n=10^6$ confirms that the bound is tight within a factor of two of the exact TVD for random probability vectors. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/kotlin-systems-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261009_053853_deterministic_approximation_of}.
